_about: Named rig profiles. `vbench_v0` is GENERATED by scripts/import_rig_geometry.py from the sibling omnimarble-vbench checkout -- do not hand-edit it; re-run the importer. `legacy_gates_v1` is frozen and deliberately defers to config/coil_params.json so the committed 300V trajectory fixture stays exactly reproducible.

legacy_gates_v1.description: The pre-hardware sim: six idealised IR gates, position-based cutoff, 470uF bank, 10mm marble. Frozen. This is the configuration the committed 300V reference trajectory was captured under, so it must keep reproducing bit-for-bit.

provenance.note: Not a description of any physical rig. The coil geometry, bank and marble here were chosen before hardware existed and disagree with the as-built rig on every count -- see the vbench_v0 profile.

marble.mass_note: derived from radius and STEEL_DENSITY_G_MM3, not measured

track.provenance: synthetic -- NOT the physical bench track

vbench_v0.description: The as-built vbench rig: measured circuit, two 5-channel IR stations, fixed on-time cutoff, 12.7mm steel ball.

provenance.note: Generated by scripts/import_rig_geometry.py -- do not hand-edit. Re-run with --check to detect upstream drift.

sensing.pitch_provenance: MEASURED off track/new-ir-board.jpeg against the ruler in shot (+/-0.5%): five packages at 22.023/22.188/21.976/22.370, mean 22.14. CONFIRMED 2026-08-01 by a null test against the printed mount, whose windows are cut at this pitch: all five packages sit hard against the same window edge, where a pitch error would instead show as a gradient along the array. That pins it to +/-0.05 mm. [RESOLVED at import: firmware/config.py reads 22.14, matching. The 'STILL SAYS 11.0' clause above is stale text hardcoded in track/rig.py.]

firing_return._note: Return leg (sustain): B's coil-nearest channel to the B-side coil face, assumed symmetric with A's (SENSOR_B_FIRST_TO_COIL_MM). The fire time is constant velocity over the last channel pair plus the EMPIRICAL trim min(trim_max, K / v_local + gate * (on_us - ref)) on top of the mirrored fire offset and the manual offset. The constant-acceleration predictor was falsified on the bench 2026-09-25: the slowing through station B is local to the station and does not continue to the coil.

pulse_measured_by_cans._note: Per-configuration LARGE-SIGNAL constants from bench blank-fire fits, R pinned at the measured ESR convention (vbench firmware/config.py BANK_*_UF_PULSE / LOOP_R_MOHM_PULSE_*). Electrolytic droop makes pulse C sub-linear in can count (C_pulse/C_100Hz = 0.859/0.931/0.958 at 1/2/3), so n x can_uF understates C by 6-8% at 2-3 cans and overstates the waveform speed exactly where the marble on-time data probes it. Configs absent here fall back to the n x can_uF scaling. The 3-can C carries a caveat: no single linear C fits that discharge (rms 0.015); 5350 is the best single-number summary.

measured.freewheel_note: Fitted 2026-09-05 from the three scope-injected marble points (400/700/1500 us gates): tau ~275 us is the unique tail that makes all three measured-current predictions agree with the marble data (ratios 1.03/1.01/1.04). Independently corroborated: it implies freewheel R ~65 mohm, which fits under the 10 V capture's model-free TOTAL loop R of 80 mohm -- whereas the 107 mohm 'coil+leads' figure above cannot (it exceeds the whole measured loop). That 107 figure is now considered wrong at pulse conditions; it remains recorded as the 1 kHz bench measurement it was. When present, this tau overrides L/R_coil for the freewheel decay.
measured.note: L by 4-wire LCR at 10kHz (Q~8; the 1kHz reading is soft at Q~1). loop_resistance is the whole discharge path and is what sets the pulse -- confirmed twice, by on-time sweep fit (0.164) and DC injection (0.161). Do not conflate it with coil_resistance, which is coil+leads only.

marble.mass_note: mass_kg MEASURED on a scale 2026-08-25 at 8.50 g. The old assumed 8.42 g came from solid-steel density and a 12.7 mm diameter; the real ball is 1.0% heavier. dv goes as 1/m, so this LOWERS every predicted dv by 0.9% -- it widens the gap to the rig rather than closing it, which is worth knowing: mass is now eliminated as an explanation for the ~1.2x under-prediction.

losses._note: The fitted loss table (scripts/fit_track_losses.py) the 1-D sustain twin runs on, embedded so the Kit extension carries the same numbers. mode 'fitted': the flat-zone drag and the B-side excess are applied as an explicit axial force in the physics step and PhysX damping is zero; 'physx': PhysX damping only (the pre-sustain behaviour). ramps 'physx': the collidable STL ramps do the excursions; 'fitted': the energy-form transfer v_back^2 = alpha v_out^2 - beta is applied at the flat edge instead, to reproduce the twin exactly.

physx_damping._note: PhysxRigidBodyAPI linear/angular damping per loss mode, 1/s. 'fitted' is zero: the forces carry the loss. 'physx' matches dv/dt = -d v to the fitted a0 + k v^2 at 0.20 m/s (the cycle speed); it is wrong everywhere else, which is why 'fitted' is the default. Angular damping is zero in both: on a rolling ball it brakes through the contact by an amount PhysX does not document, so it would be a second unfitted loss.
